Render a Figure from a Specification

Source: R/figure-spec.R
RenderFigure.Rd

Builds every panel of a figure from a declarative specification and named plot data, then composes the page. A specification is a list (or a JSON file) with height_mm, optional width_mm, panels, texts and legends. Each panel has a box ([left, top, width, height] in mm), optional letter, letter_at, heading and note, a grammar from FigureGrammars(), the name(s) of its data and builder args.

Usage

RenderFigure(spec, data = list(), style = ManuscriptStyle())

Arguments

spec

A specification list, a JSON path, several JSON paths or a directory of JSON files.

data

Named list of data frames (or other inputs) referred to by the panels.

style

A ManuscriptStyle() object; spec$style entries are applied on top.

Value

A ComposeFigure() result.

Details

Positions can also be given as fractions of the page, as in figure code that places axes with [left, bottom, width, height] fractions: a panel axes field replaces box, letter_xy replaces letter_at, and a text or legend xy replaces at (fractions measured from the bottom-left corner; letters and texts hang from the given point).

A specification may be split over several files: give a character vector of JSON paths (or a directory of *.json files). Page fields are taken from the first file that has them; panels, texts and legends are concatenated in file order.

Colours in args, texts and legends may be hex values, style colour names ("ink", "muted", ...) or palette entries written "palette/name" (for example "groups/group1"); character vectors and named lists of such values are resolved element by element. Every builder argument whose name ends in colour, color, fill or palette (or their plurals) is resolved this way, so arguments that name data columns must not end like that. The value "group" is kept as it is, for builders that colour by group (label_colour = "group").

Builders with a box_mm argument receive the size of their data area in millimetres (used for "auto" tick intervals, see NiceBreaks()).

Typesetting (TypesetLabel()) can be switched off with "typeset": false for the whole specification, for one panel (its heading, note and plot), for one text or for one legend; "typeset": {"off": ["treg"]} switches off single rules only (see TypesetLabel()).

Legends take labels, colours, shape, ncol, size and the layout options of LegendKeys() (key_mm, marker_size, row_mm, text_gap_mm, column_gap_mm, byrow). Texts take label, xy or at, size, colour, bold, hjust, vjust (a number or "baseline") and angle.

Examples

d <- data.frame(group = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3), value = c(1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 5))
spec <- list(height_mm = 50, width_mm = 70, panels = list(
  list(box = c(15, 10, 45, 30), letter = "a", heading = "Values", grammar = "group_strip",
       data = "values",
       args = list(group_colours = list(A = "groups/group1", B = "groups/group2")))))
fig <- RenderFigure(spec, list(values = d))
grid::grid.newpage(); print(fig)
